author: StewieFG
body:
Well, I know there are already posts about that, but I want this one to be serious. 
Lately I have noticed that Avicus loses players and loses popularity as well, I remember the days when it used to get 300 players, what happened to these days? The staff keep saying it's just about time and they said after the Omega update we will have more players, but I haven't noticed any difference. So I thought about making this post.
In this post I want you to say exactly, with detail, why do you think Avicus loses popularity. I am sure the staff and especially Kylo did not understand yet exactly what the players want and why it loses popularity. So in that post I want you to be serious and expalin with detail why do you think it loses popularity. 

In my opinion, it loses players because the lag and the bad gameplay it provoides sometimes, usually it used to be good and no lag at all, but after 1.8 it has all the lags back, for example block lag, invisibility players lag, spectators vision lag, etc. I saw some servers don't have these lags, which means there is way to fix it. Another reason is the in-game community, 'HAX' 'HACKER' MOD BAN THIS HACKING' 'SHUT UP NIGGA', etc. 

Note: Please, keep this post serious, mature, appropriate and don't make jokes like 'cuz the fkin block lag lololol'.

I hope Kylo and the staff will notice this post and see what the players want.
The intention is this post isn't complaining, it's for make Avicus better, so please.

replies.author: Sho
replies.body:
People are confusing robotic moderators/staff with not listening to the community and executing punishments correctly.
"omg i said a swear word in chat and he punishes me so mean"
You know what? If a moderator/staff member punishes you for saying "rekt" or "ez" in global chat or breaking the rules even in a jokingly manner he/she may be a dick but it's still doing their job. If the moderator would leave you unpunished but would punish a randy accordingly you are receiving special treatment. This is known as BIAS. Do many staff members do this? No. Why? Cuz it's violating social norms and you would hurt relationships between friends. Should they? Maybe. If you truly care about the server you should do this accordingly. It may not seem like a big deal, but this bias accumulates to the point where it is noticeable and actually poses a problem.  

Also, I do agree that the (some of )staff need to listen to the community. Why is badlion growing so much? because the staff listen. Yes there are certain lines but they are very open-minded. Im not asking to just let the community have complete control but certain staff members are not keen into taking different opinions into account. Because after all who are the most important people on the server? the players, which is what makes it grow.

replies.author: Storm997
replies.body: Personally, I think it's because we're only appealing to a certain kind of people: DTM.  It's by far the most played game, and really, it's the only played game.  Even the people you see on CTW are only on a "mix" server, so they can also play nebula.  Yeah, there's the occasional walls or CTH game, but that's only 15 people compared to the hundred on nebula.  And sure, it's popular because it's fun, but not to everyone.  I personally dislike nebula, and really love nexus, but nobody plays nexus now so I have to go play the walls.  Imagine you're joining a new server for the first time.  It looks really great, it's got all these game modes, and you say "Man, Control the Hill looks fun!" But you can't play it, because everyone's on nebula.  So, how do we fix it?  I don't know, really.  Advertising helps, but as I said above, not that much.  Personally, I think a good move would be to lower the minimum player count.  Remember when you could have a 1v1 on nexus?  Now you need 16 players, and that's never going to happen.  If I logged on one day and saw three or four people in a game, and I knew that those three or four alone were playing, I'd join them.  And that's my idea of fun.  Maybe it's not yours, but I'm really not sure what is.                                                                   tl;dr Advertise more, yes, but lower the minimum player count too.  Even if a game is small, that's better than never being able to play it, which is what we have now.

replies.author: Jake41901
replies.body:
Okay, here we go. I'm gonna go ahead and inform you all about what this decrease in player count is all about. 

Believe it or not, the transfer from McZone to Avicus was where it all started. I had no personal issues with the switch, however many players had issues with the way Avicus was run. A few rather popular mini games were removed, such as the Survival Games, and Nexus. These mini games (along with others) were removed due to the fact that the whole point of Avicus was to contain only unique mini games. However we did keep The Walls gamemode, so players lost hope in us because we had promised a completely unique plethora of game modes, and The Walls does appear on countless other servers. Nebula as well, is very similar to the Average DTM game modes in other places. Considering most of the players that left probably played on a mini game that had been removed, it explains a lot.

Secondly, (and this may seem unbelievable) but keeping the Christmas lobby for so long made some players lose hope. A lot of chatter came about, how we had kept the Christmas lobby months after the holidays. Players found it ridiculous, and inefficient. Because of this lack of progression, players began thinking that if we couldn't even change our lobby back to its original when we were supposed to, there's no way we'd make progress with development. In my opinion, that isn't true at all. However I was contacted by many players explaining their opinion, and their opinion was exactly what I just said above. They lost their will to think that we would have an efficient development system. 

Thirdly, the Avicus 2.0 Update wasn't exactly what people had hoped. When it was first released, it contained countless unfixed bugs, complications, etc. However when the Avicore update did come out, our player count rose from a steady 100-300 players back up to between 600-800 players on average. But over time, the player count consistently dropped back down to a solid 100-300 players at a time. 

And now, here we are. The Omega Update had been released only supporting 1.8, therefore causing another not very noticeable, yet impacting player drop. However because they're now going to go back to 1.7+ and begin advertising, the player count should begin to rise over time. If I missed anything, anyone can feel free to comment below and add anything in that they please, or correct me on anything I explained wrong.

Hope this cleared some things up.
